repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until(not (any(#ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == false|))
triggered = false
}
wait until(any(#ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == false|)
all(#Switch).switch_on()
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR requires a rising-edge wait on a slot declared as `any` (existential). The candidate used `all` (universal) in the wait condition, causing it to block until *both* sensors were false. Evidence F2 shows the IR acted at t=0 when only ContactSensor_1 was false, while the JoI did nothing because ContactSensor_2 was still true. The operator must be changed from `==` to `==|` to match the existential quantifier of the `any` binding slot.
diagnosis.change_summary: Changed `all(#ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == false` to `any(#ContactSensor).contactSensor_contact == false|` (or equivalently using the `|` operator on the comparison). This aligns the JoI condition with the `any` binding slot in the IR, allowing the action to fire as soon as at least one sensor reports false, matching the rising-edge semantics.
